To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) anthelmintic compounds of the class of macrolides are potent anti-cancer agents; (ii) anthelmintics induce apoptosis in leukemia cells through mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization and (iii) anthelmintices synergize with other drugs that target the same cell death machinery.
we have identified anti-leukemia activities of anthelmintics, which are used as anti-parasitic drugs.

we performed a drug screening of 2487 FDA approved drugs in leukemia cells and discovered that anthelmintic drugs are highly effective against leukemia cells and may be used as novel treatment for leukemia.

the development of new drugs to treat cancer, in particular acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL).
the discovery of new therapeutic agents for the treatment of leukemia and the identification of new targets for the treatment of cancer.
the identification of new anti-leukemia drugs.

the use of anthelmintics for the treatment of leukemia is a promising approach.
anthelmintic drugs have the potential to be used as anti-leukemia drugs.

we have identified an anti-leukemia drug activity in a drug screen and that this activity was validated in primary leukemia samples.
anthelmintic drugs are repurposed to eradicate leukemia, including relapse and drug-resistant cases.
